nodes.name: Precursor drying and calcination
nodes.procedure: Na₂MoO₄-dopamine mixture precursor ink was dried, followed by calcination at 800°C for 2 h in Ar (g) atmosphere. This resulted in the formation of 3D solid pompon-like Mo₂C particles with diameters in the range of 600-900 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern shows two sets of diffraction peaks corresponding to hexagonal Mo₂C (JCPDS 35-0787) and cubic Mo₂N (JCPDS 25-1366) with no discernible impurities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of the material (Figure 2a) showed two sets of diffraction peaks corresponding to hexagonal Mo₂C (JCPDS 35-0787) and cubic Mo₂N (JCPDS 25-1366). No discernible impurities were found by XRD.

properties.description: X-ray diffraction pattern with peaks labeled against reference cards

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show 3D solid pompon-like morphology of Mo₂C-Mo₂N heterostructures with diameters in the range of 600-900 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscope (SEM) images were taken to study the morphology of the Mo₂C-Mo₂N heterostructures which presented a 3D solid pompon-like shape with diameters in the range of 600-900 nm (Figure 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals Mo₂C-Mo₂N heterostructures consist of numerous nanosheets of ≈10 atom-thickness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscope (TEM) and spherical aberration-corrected transmission electron microscope (ACTEM) provide us with further insight into the structure of the materials at the nanoscale. The 3D solid pompon-like Mo₂C-Mo₂N heterostructures consist of numerous nanosheets of ≈10 atom-thickness (Figure 2c, 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: ACTEM images evidence excellent lattice matching at the interfaces between Mo₂C and Mo₂N components.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRACTEM images also evidence an excellent lattice matching at the interfaces between Mo₂C and Mo₂N components (Figure 2e, 2f).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM and corresponding elemental mappings confirm that Mo, C, and N are distributed uniformly in the Mo₂C-Mo₂N heterostructures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and the corresponding elemental mappings confirm that Mo, C, and N are distributed uniformly in the Mo₂C-Mo₂N heterostructures (Figure 2i).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show Mo₂N vibration mode at 587.2 cm⁻¹ and Mo₂C vibration modes at 846.3 cm⁻¹ and 1020.8 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a displays the Raman spectra of Mo₂C, Mo₂N, and Mo₂C-Mo₂N heterostructures. The vibration mode of Mo₂N locates at 587.2 cm⁻¹ and the vibration modes located at 846.3 cm⁻¹ and 1020.8 cm⁻¹ are corresponding to Mo₂C.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Mo 3d₅/₂ Mo-C peak at 228.9 eV (shifted from 229.0 eV in Mo₂C), Mo-N peak at 229.4 eV (shifted from 229.1 eV in Mo₂N), Mo₂C/Mo₂N content ratio of 1.50; only Mo, O, C, N elements present.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Mo 3d₅/₂ spectrum of Mo₂C locates at 229.0 eV (Figure S9a), and the Mo 3d₅/₂ spectrum of Mo₂N locates at 229.1 eV (Figure S10a)... Compared to Mo₂C, the Mo-C peak of Mo₂C-Mo₂N slightly shifts to a lower binding energy of 228.9 eV (Figure 3b) whereas the Mo–N peak of Mo₂C-Mo₂N shifts to a higher binding energy of 229.4 eV. ... the content ratio of Mo₂C/Mo₂N of the Mo₂C-Mo₂N is 1.50 based on the XPS fitting results.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM image identifies obvious interface via height difference between Mo₂C and Mo₂N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3e, an obvious interface can be identified via height difference in the AFM image.

nodes.characterization_summary: KPFM shows potential of Mo₂C higher than Mo₂N, indicating electrons transfer from Mo₂C to Mo₂N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be found that the potential of Mo₂C is higher than that of the Mo₂N in the KPFM image (Figure 3e).

nodes.characterization_summary: NH₃-TPD curve for Mo₂C shows physical adsorption peak at 100°C and chemical adsorption peak at 735°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the NH₃ temperature-programmed diagram (NH₃-TPD) curve for Mo₂C, the peak located at 100°C corresponds to the unstable physical adsorption of NH₃, while the chemical adsorption of NH₃ on the Mo₂C starts from 600°C and attains peak value at 735°C (Figure S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical double layer capacitance Cdl = 19.2 mF cm⁻² in acid (highest among catalysts), indicating largest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The well lattice-matched Mo₂C-Mo₂N heterostructures exhibit the highest Cdl value of 19.2 mF cm⁻², compared to that of Mo₂C (11.3 mF cm⁻²) and Mo₂N (6.8 mF cm⁻²) electrocatalysts (Figure S15).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows smallest charge transfer resistance Rct = 51.3 Ω in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ (vs Mo₂C: 69.7 Ω, Mo₂N: 85.6 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S18a presents the Nyquist plots of the electrocatalysts in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ and the Mo₂C-Mo₂N shows the smallest Rct of 51.3 Ω compared with that of the Mo₂C (69.7 Ω), Mo₂N (85.6 Ω)...
